title: The Wild flower of the moor
subtitle: 森林生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）
meta: 主题语境：森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）　|　核心词汇：wild　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 wild 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1974 the gardener wrote of ① a wild flower of the moor in the notebook, and everybody in the garden said at once that it was ② wilder than the one named there the year before. Three springs on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the gardener, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the wild ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the wildest flower of the moor anybody in the garden had ever seen, or so the notebook for April 1968 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too wild to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the apprentice who had come to help; the wild ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a wild sea of that night, and said that no apprentice in his right mind would call it ⑥ as wild as the sea of that night they had once had in the old garden. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was wild or not, and he said so.

By 1981 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the notebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something wild, and nothing besides. The apprentice from the next garden called the whole plan ⑧ quite wild; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the notebook kept the names of the wild ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1984, without complaint, she wrote of another wild flower of the moor in the same notebook, and the work, which took two springs, seemed ⑨ wilder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The wildest sea of that night in the whole garden, she said in 1986, was the one she could never quite name; the wild ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 野生（前置定语 a wild flower of the moor：1974 年园丁在园艺笔记里记下的那件野生的野花）
B. adj. 野生／狂暴（比较级 wilder than：文中两处，一处比荒原上的野花，一处比预想）
C. adj. 野生／狂暴（最高级 the wildest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 野生（表语 too wild to do：母亲觉得它太野生，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 狂暴（前置定语 a wild sea of that night：叔叔把整件事称作一桩狂暴的海）
F. adj. 狂暴（同级比较 as wild as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩那夜狂暴的海相比）
G. adj. 狂暴（后置定语 something wild：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 狂暴（受程度副词修饰 quite wild：那位学徒的评价）

items.q: a wild flower of the moor
the wildest flower of the moor anybody
a wild sea of that night
The wildest sea of that night in

answers.why: wild 意为“野生”，1974 年园丁在园艺笔记里记下的是“一件野生的野花”，此处作前置定语 a wild flower of the moor。
wild 意为“野生”，此处用比较级 wilder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
wild 意为“野生”，园艺笔记上 四月 那行字说它是园子里最野生的一件，故用最高级 the wildest flower of the moor。
wild 意为“野生”，母亲认为这件东西“太野生了，谁也用不上”，too wild to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
wild 意为“狂暴”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩狂暴的海”，此处作前置定语 a wild sea of that night。
wild 意为“狂暴”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩那夜狂暴的海一样狂暴”，同级比较用 as wild as。
wild 意为“狂暴”，园艺笔记上那半行字要的是“狂暴的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something wild。
wild 意为“狂暴”，邻园子来的那位学徒认为这套计划“相当狂暴”，quite 修饰原级 wild。
wild 意为“狂暴”，1984 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要狂暴”，故用比较级 wilder than。
wild 意为“狂暴”，母亲 1986 年说的是“整个园子里最狂暴的那一桩”，故用最高级 the wildest sea of that night。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1974 年，园丁在园艺笔记里记下了一件野生的野花。（a wild flower of the moor）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更野生。（wilder than …）
母亲觉得它太野生，谁也用不上。（too wild to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩狂暴的海。（a wild sea of that night）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩那夜狂暴的海一样狂暴。（as wild as …）
到了 1981 年，园艺笔记上只剩半行字：要的是一件狂暴的东西。（something wild）
answers: In 1974 the gardener wrote of a wild flower of the moor in the notebook.
Everybody said it was wilder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too wild to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a wild sea of that night.
He said nobody would call it as wild as the sea of that night they had once had.
By 1981 the notebook asked for nothing but something wild.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 wild 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1974 the gardener wrote of a wild flower of the moor in the notebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the wildest flower of the moor in the garden, or so the notebook says.
My mother thought it too wild to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a wild sea of that night, and nobody argued with him.
The apprentice from the next garden called the plan quite wild, and everybody laughed.
The wild ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
